display.purpose: Phase headings, review headings, and strongest current-context statements.

title.purpose: Section prompts and compact group headings.

label.purpose: Journey steps and compact status labels.

motion.name: action-arrive
motion.purpose: One-time clipped reveal for a newly available dominant action; disabled under reduced motion.

components.name: Primary Next Action
components.description: The single dominant action for the current journey state.
components.css: .ds-primary-action { position: relative; width: 100%; min-height: 116px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 24px 86px 24px clamp(22px, 7vw, 52px); border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: var(--accent, #ffd400); color: var(--text-h, #050505); font: 700 clamp(1.9rem, 8vw, 3rem)/1 var(--heading, sans-serif); letter-spacing: -0.02em; text-align: left; text-transform: uppercase; animation: ds-action-arrive 420ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; } .ds-primary-action::after { position: absolute; top: 50%; right: 32px; width: 34px; height: 34px; border-top: 10px solid currentColor; border-right: 10px solid currentColor; content: ''; transform: translateY(-50%) rotate(45deg); } .ds-primary-action:hover { background: #050505; color: var(--accent, #ffd400); } .ds-primary-action:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #1261a0; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-primary-action:active { filter: brightness(0.92); } @keyframes ds-action-arrive { from { clip-path: inset(0 5% 0 0); filter: brightness(0.9); } to { clip-path: inset(0); filter: brightness(1); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-primary-action { animation: none; } }

components.name: Secondary Action
components.description: A quiet alternative or recovery action that does not compete with the next action.
components.css: .ds-secondary-action { min-height: 52px; padding: 12px 16px; border: 1px solid #101010; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: #101010; font: 700 18px/1.4 var(--heading, sans-serif); } .ds-secondary-action:hover { background: #050505; color: #ffffff; } .ds-secondary-action:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #1261a0; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-secondary-action:active { filter: brightness(0.88); }

components.name: Planning Constraint
components.description: A factual optional constraint using a native checkbox and explicit selected state.
components.css: .ds-constraint { display: flex; min-height: 48px; box-sizing: border-box; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid #101010; border-radius: 0; background: #ffffff; color: #101010; font: 700 18px/1.4 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', sans-serif; } .ds-constraint:hover { background: #fff2a8; } .ds-constraint:has(input:checked) { background: var(--accent, #ffd400); } .ds-constraint input { width: 22px; height: 22px; accent-color: #050505; } .ds-constraint input:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #1261a0; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Journey Progress
components.description: The persistent four-step Plan, Perform, Cooldown, Review orientation path.
components.css: .ds-journey { overflow: hidden; background: #050505; color: #ffffff; } .ds-journey ol { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); margin: 0; padding: 18px 12px 16px; list-style: none; } .ds-journey li { position: relative; display: grid; min-width: 0; justify-items: center; gap: 8px; color: #ffffff; font: 700 0.72rem/1 var(--heading, sans-serif); letter-spacing: 0.03em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-journey li::before { position: absolute; top: 9px; right: 50%; left: -50%; height: 2px; background: #ffffff; content: ''; } .ds-journey li:first-child::before { display: none; } .ds-journey li span { z-index: 1; width: 16px; height: 16px; box-sizing: border-box; border: 3px solid #ffffff; border-radius: 50%; background: #050505; } .ds-journey li[aria-current='step'] { color: var(--accent, #ffd400); } .ds-journey li[aria-current='step'] span { border-color: var(--accent, #ffd400); background: var(--accent, #ffd400); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #050505, 0 0 0 5px var(--accent, #ffd400); }

components.name: Exercise Row
components.description: A reachable alternate exercise with its identity, progress, timing, and disclosure state.
components.css: .ds-exercise-row { display: grid; width: 100%; min-height: 78px; grid-template-columns: 62px minmax(0, 1fr) auto; gap: 14px; align-items: center; padding: 12px clamp(16px, 5vw, 32px); border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #101010; border-radius: 0; background: #ffffff; color: #101010; text-align: left; } .ds-exercise-row:hover { background: #fff2a8; } .ds-exercise-row:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #1261a0; outline-offset: -4px; background: #fff2a8; } .ds-exercise-number { font: 700 2.5rem/1 var(--heading, sans-serif); letter-spacing: -0.04em; } .ds-exercise-name { display: grid; min-width: 0; font: 700 1.15rem/1.2 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', sans-serif; } .ds-exercise-name small { color: #5a5a5a; font-size: 0.8rem; } .ds-exercise-status { max-width: 18ch; color: #454545; font: 400 0.78rem/1.4 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', sans-serif; text-align: right; } @media (max-width: 520px) { .ds-exercise-row { grid-template-columns: 52px minmax(0, 1fr); } .ds-exercise-status { grid-column: 2; max-width: none; text-align: left; } }

components.name: Set Input
components.description: A large numeric field for set performance details.
components.css: .ds-set-input { display: grid; gap: 6px; color: #101010; font: 700 0.9rem/1.2 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', sans-serif; } .ds-set-input input { width: 100%; min-height: 58px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid #101010; border-radius: 0; background: #ffffff; color: #101010; font: 700 1.6rem/1.2 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', sans-serif; } .ds-set-input input:hover { background: #fff2a8; } .ds-set-input input:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #1261a0; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Settings Field
components.description: An explicitly labeled native field with adjacent validation feedback.
components.css: .ds-settings-field { display: grid; gap: 8px; color: #050505; font: 400 18px/1.4 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', sans-serif; } .ds-settings-field input { min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid #101010; border-radius: 0; background: #ffffff; color: #050505; } .ds-settings-field input:hover { background: #fff2a8; } .ds-settings-field input:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #1261a0; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-settings-field input[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: #721c24; } .ds-settings-field small { padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid #721c24; background: #ffffff; color: #721c24; }

narrative.overview:
Nudge is a high-contrast operating interface for a trainee using a phone around equipment. Hard-edged black, white, pale-concrete, and signal-yellow planes establish context quickly; generous identifiers and condensed headings make the current state legible without decoration or motivational theater.

The system applies to the shared shell, the approved Plan → Perform → Cooldown → Review journey, the read-only Workout history disclosure, and Settings with its exercise catalog. Every active state answers three questions in order: what is happening, what is the one dominant next action, and which other exercises remain available. Guidance comes from hierarchy and plain language, never literal route, gate, airport, or destination terminology.
keyCharacteristics: One unmistakable signal-yellow next action per state
Flat, hard-edged planes separated by thin rules
Condensed, oversized state labels paired with highly legible body copy
Mobile-first stacking with alternatives present but visually quieter
Calm, factual language that preserves trainee agency

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow identifies the current state or the one dominant next action; do not distribute it across competing controls.

rules.name: The Structural Contrast Rule
rules.body: Use black, white, concrete, and thin rules to separate regions before introducing any additional color.

rules.name: The State Before Detail Rule
rules.body: Lead with the phase, action, timer, or exercise identifier; supporting explanation follows in body type.

rules.name: The One Page Heading Rule
rules.body: The shared Nudge wordmark is the page’s sole first-level heading; each active surface or workout state begins at the second level without changing its visual scale.

rules.name: The Decision Order Rule
rules.body: Place current context first, the dominant next action second, and alternate exercises or disclosures after it.

rules.name: The Flat Signal Rule
rules.body: Do not use shadows to manufacture importance; use plane contrast, rules, and scale.

dos: Do make one worthwhile next action unmistakable in every journey state.
Do keep other exercises visible and reachable without asking the trainee to re-plan.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, readable timing and status, reduced-motion behavior, and phone-sized touch targets.
Do keep settings controls explicitly labeled and keep warning, error, loading, and mutation feedback adjacent to the affected region.
Do use plain labels such as “Exercises,” “Start set,” “Cooldown,” and “Review.”
donts: Don't use route, gate, destination, next-stop, or other literal airport terminology.
Don't introduce streak pressure, guilt, gamification, faux precision, unsupported readiness, invented recommendations, or authoritative coaching.
Don't turn Settings or the catalog into a separate visual language of rounded cards, decorative badges, or competing accent actions.
Don't make alternate actions compete in scale, color, or placement with the dominant next action.
